tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand the local, single-user Computer Use workbench and its three supported provider routes. It establishes the safety boundary and the major backend, sandbox, and dashboard components explored next.

tour.title: Runtime Startup
tour.description: The backend entry point applies the local-network guardrail and starts the FastAPI application. It is the first code stop because it establishes the runtime boundary described in the overview.

tour.title: V2 API Contract
tour.description: The typed v2 API defines session, credential, workflow, audit, and retention operations used by the dashboard. Read it after startup to see how HTTP requests become managed Computer Use executions.

tour.title: Execution Coordination
tour.description: The orchestrator owns active tasks and subscriber notifications for each session. Together with the API it explains how a request transitions into an observable asynchronous run.

tour.title: Durable Audit State
tour.description: The SQLite store persists sessions, actions, events, metrics, workflows, and checkpoints. This makes the workbench reviewable after a live run instead of relying solely on process memory.

tour.title: Dashboard Entry
tour.description: The React entry point mounts the workbench dashboard, while App composes its live, audit, workflow, provider, and analytics views. This is the browser-side counterpart to the v2 API contract.

tour.title: Browser Communication
tour.description: The API client carries typed HTTP requests and the live-stream hook maintains session events and preview frames. These files show how the dashboard consumes the session lifecycle introduced earlier.

tour.title: Operator Workflow
tour.description: The operator guide ties the application layers together into installation, provider setup, safety, dashboard, and troubleshooting procedures. Use it to connect the internal architecture with the intended user workflow.

tour.title: Sandbox Container
tour.description: The Dockerfile packages the isolated desktop action environment, and Compose connects it to the local workbench runtime. This is the containment boundary for OS input rather than an ordinary application deployment.
tour.languageLesson: Docker build layers cache stable dependency steps before application changes; Compose then defines how the sandbox service is run locally.

tour.title: Quality Gates
tour.description: The CI workflow runs the repository's automated quality and security checks before delivery. It closes the tour by showing how the documented contracts are kept from regressing.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions organize automation into triggers, jobs, and ordered steps, while pyproject.toml centralizes Python tool configuration.
